key_insight: The paper compares direct and indirect PINN formulations for Dirichlet boundary control of semilinear parabolic PDEs, and proves a conditional error analysis for the indirect approach.
engineering_relevance: It offers a principled way to train PINNs for PDE-constrained optimal control problems while quantifying how approximation, optimization, quadrature, and soft-constraint errors affect solution quality.
method: Direct PINN: separate networks for state and control, trained on a penalized tracking objective.
Indirect PINN: joint networks for state, adjoint, and control trained on the first-order optimality system.
Error framework: decomposes total error and derives a conditional residual-to-error estimate with a computable indicator.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments on two manufactured test problems—a cubic reaction-diffusion case and a linear case with nontrivial boundary control and adjoint—to compare direct and indirect formulations.
watch_item: The main error guarantee is conditional on regularity, network approximation, soft-constraint residual control, and staying in a local neighborhood of the reference optimality-system solution.
paper_title: Direct and Indirect Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Dirichlet Boundary Control of Semilinear Parabolic Equations: A Conditional Error Analysis
